paper.title: Language Generation in the Limit
paper.summary: Introduces generation in the limit from exact positive presentations and proves countable-family generation, a stronger uniform guarantee for finite families, and prompted extensions.

formalization_scope.summary: The central countable-family result has Nat-specialized semantic, observed-set, NeurIPS finite-query, and arXiv-v1 finite-query paths. A cross-paper P02 theorem covers the semantic uniform-fresh core of the finite-family result, while its fixed-sample pairwise-output conclusion and every P01 prompted result remain unformalized.
specializations: The formalized universe is Nat rather than an arbitrary explicitly enumerable countable universe.
Lean uses zero-based language and universe indices.
gaps: No arbitrary-countable-universe transport theorem is provided.
The fixed-sample membership-query realization and infinite pairwise-distinct output sequence of finite-family uniform Theorem 2.2 are not formalized.
P01 robust and non-trivial prompted generation are not formalized.
The informal pairwise-distinct-output modification of the P01 constructions is not formalized; P39 proves non-repetition for a materially different patient machine.

claims.title: Countable-family generation in the limit
claims.statement_summary: For every countably indexed family of infinite languages with uniform membership access, one target-independent algorithm eventually outputs a fresh element of the hidden target after every exact positive presentation of that target.

source_refs.notes: The arXiv-v1 machine uses a first-fresh-eligible stopping rule rather than the proceedings endpoint rule.

source_assessment.notes: The two editions state the same high-level theorem but realize it with different finite-query stopping rules.

formalization.notes: All four registered paths prove the Nat specialization. The source's arbitrary explicitly enumerable countable universe has no generic transport theorem in the P01 development.

components.summary: Countable-family generation in the limit over Nat, with both source-edition finite-query machines and two semantic interfaces.
Transport the concrete Nat constructions to every explicitly enumerable countable universe in the source theorem.

lean_links.notes: Implements the proceedings endpoint-search algorithm without receiving the target index or a convergence threshold.
Implements the literal arXiv-v1 whole-prefix stopping rule; at each successful round, leastness is only within the selected finite-critical prefix, not global in the target.
Mirrors the round-dependent Section 4 construction with time supplied explicitly; it is not the finite-query implementation of Theorem 2.1.
Supplies the literal observed-set semantic route, using distinct-observation cardinality as the candidate scope.

relations.notes: Both establish the same eventual validity/freshness criterion through different interfaces; the finite-query machines do not depend on the SetInterface construction.

claims.title: Uniform finite-family generation
claims.statement_summary: For every finite family there is a family-dependent sample bound after which one algorithm can produce an infinite pairwise-distinct sequence of fresh target elements, uniformly over the target and the sufficiently large finite sample.

source_assessment.notes: The theorem is shared by both source editions.

formalization.notes: The native P01 development omits Theorem 2.2. Cross-paper declaration GenLimit.LiRamanTewari.theorem_2_5 proves the generic finite-class uniform fresh-generation core, but not P01's fixed-sample membership-query realization or its infinite pairwise-distinct output sequence.

components.summary: One generator and one family-dependent distinct-sample threshold give persistent fresh target outputs uniformly over every target in a finite class.
A P01-style membership-query procedure generates from an arbitrary fixed sufficiently large finite target sample.
The procedure returns an infinite sequence of pairwise-distinct elements of the target outside the fixed sample.

lean_links.notes: A cross-paper P02 theorem packages the uniform fresh-output core through finite-class closure; it neither constructs the P01 membership-query algorithm nor returns an infinite pairwise-distinct sequence from one fixed sample.

relations.notes: This is the finite-family theorem with a stronger family-uniform threshold and output-sequence guarantee.

audit_refs.scope: Source inventory establishing the full force of Theorem 2.2 and its absence from the native P01 development; the registry separately records the later cross-paper P02 core.

claims.title: Finite-set semantic generation function
claims.statement_summary: Every countable family admits a semantic function of the observed finite set alone that is eventually fresh and correct along every exact presentation of a target language.

source_assessment.notes: The literal claim is retained, but the published round-dependent construction (4.5) is not itself a function of the observed set when repetitions occur. Lean supplies a cardinality-scope repair.

formalization.notes: The repetition-tolerant theorem proves the literal observed-set conclusion over Nat and repairs the paper's round-versus-set construction mismatch. No generic transport theorem covers the source's arbitrary explicitly enumerable countable universe.

components.summary: A repetition-tolerant finite-set-only semantic generation function over Nat.
Transport the finite-set-only construction to every explicitly enumerable countable universe in the source claim.

lean_links.notes: Uses the number of distinct observations rather than elapsed time as the candidate scope.
Adds injectivity so the observed-set cardinality equals the elapsed round.
Receives the elapsed round separately and therefore mirrors (4.5) without realizing the literal finite-set-only interface.

relations.notes: Both establish the same eventual validity/freshness criterion through different interfaces; the finite-query machines do not depend on the SetInterface construction.

claims.title: Robust-prompt generation
claims.statement_summary: Given an exact target presentation and prompts robust for every candidate language, a membership-query algorithm eventually returns a fresh target string extending each current prompt.

source_assessment.notes: The robust-prompt result is shared by both editions.

formalization.notes: The library has no P01 string/concatenation/prefix prompt model, robustness predicate, or matching prompted generator. P02's multiclass prompted interface is materially different.

relations.notes: Adds a prompt-extension requirement to fresh target generation.

audit_refs.scope: Source inventory and omission analysis for robust-prompt Theorem 7.1 in both editions.

claims.title: Non-trivial prompts with regular subset queries
claims.statement_summary: With membership queries and regular-subset queries, an algorithm eventually handles every prompt that currently has at least one fresh continuation in the hidden target.

source_assessment.notes: This stronger prompted result appears only in arXiv v1.

formalization.notes: No P01 string/prefix continuation model, regular-language type, or regular-subset-query oracle is present; P02's multiclass prompted interface does not supply these objects.

relations.notes: Handles a broader class of prompts while assuming a stronger query interface.

audit_refs.scope: Source inventory and omission analysis for arXiv-v1 equations (7.4)--(7.6).

claims.title: Context-free-language prompted-generation corollary
claims.statement_summary: For a family of context-free languages, the non-trivial-prompt result needs no additional regular-subset oracle because the required inclusion test is decidable using standard closure and emptiness facts.

source_assessment.notes: The corollary appears only in arXiv v1.

formalization.notes: The library has no P01 string/prefix prompt model or the regular/context-free syntax and decision procedures used by this corollary.

relations.notes: Instantiates the regular-subset-query theorem for context-free languages.

audit_refs.scope: Source inventory and omission analysis for the arXiv-v1 context-free corollary.

claims.title: No finite uniform bound for prompted generation
claims.statement_summary: Even for a family of two languages, no family-dependent finite sample bound guarantees correct prompted generation for every valid prompt after that many distinct target examples.

source_assessment.notes: This negative result appears only in arXiv v1.

formalization.notes: No P01 string/prefix prompted-generation model or two-language parity/prefix counterexample is present in Lean; P02's prompted model is different.

relations.notes: Rules out the finite-family uniform-threshold analogue of robust prompted generation.

audit_refs.scope: Source inventory and omission analysis for the arXiv-v1 prompted impossibility result.

claims.title: Pairwise-distinct generated-output strengthening
claims.statement_summary: The semantic and finite-query constructions can reportedly be modified so that generated outputs are pairwise distinct, not merely fresh relative to the adversary's observed sample.

source_assessment.notes: The strengthening is stated informally rather than as a numbered theorem.

formalization.notes: The registered P01 constructions require freshness only relative to the adversary sample and have not been extended with output history. P39 proves non-repetition for a materially different patient machine, so it is related evidence rather than a formalization of this construction-modification claim.

lean_links.notes: A different patient-scope machine proves eventual target validity, sample freshness, output non-repetition, and a lower-density bound.
Proves injectivity of the P39 output stream independently of the P01 algorithms.

relations.notes: Strengthens the output specification; no strict separation is claimed.
